root_cause.text: `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()` in the IPv6 ancillary-data path let repeated `IPV6_DSTOPTS`/`IPV6_HOPOPTS`/`IPV6_RTHDR` cmsgs overwrite the stored option pointers while only incrementing the 16-bit `ipv6_txoptions::opt_flen/opt_nflen`, so the length accounting could wrap and become smaller than the actual header copied later.
root_cause.evidence: The patch says `opt_flen`/`opt_nflen` are adjusted to “correctly reflect the size of the current option headers” by subtracting the old `dst1opt`, `dst0opt`, or `srcrt` length before adding the new one; the diff shows the old code only did `opt->opt_flen += len; opt->dst1opt = hdr;` and similar for `opt_nflen`, which allowed overflow/mismatch and led to insufficient skb headroom before `ipv6_push_exthdr()` used the full header length.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new IPv6 routing header pointer variable in `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()` for subsequent use.
intent_record.what: A new local pointer declaration, `struct ipv6_rt_hdr *orthdr;`, was added alongside the existing `rthdr` and `hdr` variables in `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()`.
intent_record.how: This change only introduces an additional variable declaration at this point in the function; by itself it does not alter control flow or runtime behavior, but it prepares the function to reference an additional IPv6 routing header pointer later in the code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix IPv6 destination-options length accounting when replacing existing control-message options.
intent_record.what: In ip6_datagram_send_ctl(), when processing an IPV6_DSTOPTS control message, the code now subtracts the IPv6 option length of any existing dst1opt from opt_flen before adding the new length and replacing dst1opt. Likewise, when processing the other destination-options case, it now subtracts the IPv6 option length of any existing dst0opt from opt_nflen before adding the new length and replacing dst0opt.
intent_record.how: This changes the accounting for IPv6 destination options so that replacing an existing option no longer leaves the old option's length counted in the running totals. At runtime, the per-flow and per-non-flow option length fields stay consistent with the currently installed option data, preventing cumulative overcounting when options are updated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix IPv6 datagram control option length accounting when replacing existing routing and destination headers.
intent_record.what: In ip6_datagram_send_ctl(), the code now saves the previous routing header from opt->srcrt into orthdr and, if present, subtracts its header length from opt->opt_nflen before adding the new routing header length and assigning opt->srcrt = rthdr. In the IPV6_2292RTHDR path, when opt->dst1opt is present, it now conditionally subtracts the length of opt->dst0opt from opt->opt_nflen before adding the dst1 header length and shifting dst1opt into dst0opt.
intent_record.how: This adjusts the net-length bookkeeping for IPv6 control options when replacing an existing routing header or destination options header, preventing the accumulated options length from incorrectly counting old headers that are being superseded. At runtime, the resulting packet option length reflects the final set of headers actually attached to the datagram.

Fix IPv6 datagram control option length accounting when replacing existing routing and destination headers.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix IPv6 datagram control option length accounting when replacing existing routing and destination headers.

relevance_review.reason: The change is in `ip6_datagram_send_ctl()` and adds a routing header pointer used in the ancillary-data handling path, which is directly part of the code path implicated by the overwrite/length-accounting bug involving repeated IPv6 cmsgs.

The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes IPv6 datagram ancillary-control option length accounting when repeated IPV6_DSTOPTS/IPV6_HOPOPTS/IPV6_RTHDR messages replace stored option pointers, preventing the length counters from becoming inconsistent and wrapping.

candidates.rationale: This increments only the 16-bit front-header length while replacing/storing the new header pointer in a way that can be repeated by multiple cmsgs, allowing the length counter to wrap and no longer match the actual copied header data.

This has the same wraparound risk for non-front headers: repeated ancillary options can keep overwriting stored pointers while only increasing the length field, eventually making the recorded length smaller than the real payload copied later.

Overwriting the stored destination-options pointer on repeated IPV6_DSTOPTS cmsgs is part of the bug: the pointer changes while the length bookkeeping just accumulates, so later copying can use a header size that no longer matches the accounting.
This pointer overwrite for the alternate destination-options path contributes to the mismatch between stored option content and the incremented 16-bit length fields.
This is the length-accounting operation for routing-header insertion; repeated cmsgs could make the non-front length wrap, which is the root cause of the mismatch described.

vuln_statements.explanation: This increments only the 16-bit front-header length while repeated ancillary options can overwrite the stored header pointer, allowing the length field to wrap and become inconsistent with the actual copied data.
This is the non-front-header length accounting that can wrap under repeated cmsgs while option pointers are replaced, causing the recorded length to no longer match the real header payload.
Overwriting the stored destination-options pointer on repeated IPV6_DSTOPTS cmsgs is part of the vulnerability because it lets the payload change while only the length counter is accumulated.
This alternate destination-options pointer overwrite contributes to the mismatch between stored option content and the incremented 16-bit length fields.
